entities.summary: The Duchy of Saxony was a medieval duchy that was encompassing the Old Saxony, a historical region settled by the Saxons since the Migration Period. Initially independent, it came under the sphere of influence of the neighboring Frankish rulers already during the Merovingian era. It was later subdued by Charlemagne during the Saxon Wars (772-804), and incorporated into the Carolingian Empire. Since the Treaty of Verdun (843), it belonged to the East Frankish Kingdom, and thus became one of the five stem duchies of the emerging German realm.
